title: intermittent first-byte and throughput sag during multi-tenant model fanout
creator: Maya Patel
description: Multiple customers in EU and US reported intermittent first-byte delays and sustained tokens/sec degradation when their requests fan out across multiple model variants (chat-extended, adm-20k). Symptoms: elevated TTFT (first byte) spikes of 150-600ms above baseline for a subset of requests, followed by steady-state tokens/sec dropping by ~30-40% for 30–120s windows. Issue appears in Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments but is most apparent under multi-tenant consolidation and when the new batching estimator and kernel-selection heuristics from runtime-1.18 are active. Customer impact includes timeouts on sync endpoints and increased error rates on streaming consumers.
comments: 2026-03-12 - Maya Patel: Escalation received from CustA (EU) reporting 3x higher TTFT during bursts. Support attached p50/p95 traces and a customer load profile. Triage call scheduled.

2026-03-12 - Liam O'Connor: Initial triage shows correlation with model fanout (requests routed to 1-3 model variants). Observed reduced batch sizes and frequent kernel warmup events. Reproduced locally with synthetic fanout generator against a 4x model set at 80% concurrency.

2026-03-13 - Performance lab: Reproduced tokens/sec sag when batching-estimator window drops below 12ms for incoming streams. Hypothesis: estimator overshoots and forces micro-batches; combined with aggressive KV eviction from new gc tuning leads to cache misses and kernel underutilization.

2026-03-13 - Mitigation applied: rolled kernel-selection heuristic back on a canary pool and disabled aggressive KV GC for canary nodes. Early canary shows TTFT p95 improvement of ~230ms and tokens/sec regained to within 10% of baseline.
2026-03-13 - Customer comms: Support sent interim report to CustA/CustB and enabled per-route conservative batching (force-min-batch 16) as temporary workaround for affected routes.

2026-03-14 - Engineering plan: implement two-pronged hotfix - (1) batching-estimator guardrails to avoid sub-12ms windows, (2) KV cache GC backoff and sticky affinity enforcement for multi-model fanout requests. Prepare runtime-1.18.1-hotfix branch. Target rollout to Dedicated canaries today, Hosted EU tomorrow, Private customers offered a patch package.
2026-03-14 - PRs: opened runtime PR #7821 (estimator guardrails) and runtime PR #7824 (kv-gc backoff + affinity override). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7821
2026-03-14 - Ops note: add telemetry metric 'fanout_batch_size' and new alert for sustained tokens/sec drop >25% for >60s. Add dashboard tile to Console for affected customers.
2026-03-14 - Blockers: need rapid sign-off from infra on affinity changes for Dedicated; Private customer testing windows scheduled with SEs.

2026-03-14 - Next steps: complete unit/integration tests, run 8h perf ramp in lab, deploy canary + monitor 2h, then schedule rolling hotfix for Hosted EU and Dedicated after verification. Update customers with post-mitigation timeline.
